subject: Student Transportation Cost Policy
overview: The committee reviewed the fiscal year 2022 budget for the central office and facilities, detailing infrastructure repairs and a reorganization of family engagement services. A motion passed to ensure that students living more than two miles from school will no longer pay for transportation.

items.title: Budget Timeline and Fiscal Overview
items.summary: David Murphy presented the budget development timeline and estimated a necessary funding increase of between $3.4 million and $5.8 million, driven by contractual obligations and collective bargaining.

items.title: Buildings and Grounds Infrastructure Priorities
items.summary: John McLaughlin outlined urgent infrastructure needs, including transformer and generator replacements at the high school, boiler repairs at Curtis Tufts, and restroom rehabilitation.

items.title: Professional Development and Training
items.summary: District leaders discussed investments in social-emotional learning, implicit bias training, and anti-racist initiatives using a 'train-the-trainer' model to ensure long-term sustainability.

items.title: Central Office Reorganization and Grant Management
items.summary: The administration proposed merging the Parent Information Center and before-school programs into a single Family Engagement office and confirmed the appointment of a dedicated grant coordinator.

items.title: Extracurricular Equity and Restroom Facilities
items.summary: Member Ruseau requested data on the equitable distribution of transportation funding between athletics and music programs and advocated for free menstrual product dispensers in all renovated bathrooms.

items.title: Elimination of Student Transportation Fees
items.summary: The committee approved a motion requiring the FY22 budget to assume no out-of-pocket costs for students residing outside the two-mile radius who currently use MBTA passes to reach school.

items.title: High School Vision and Capital Planning
items.summary: The committee debated the timing of high school renovations, with some members calling for a comprehensive master plan and the reconvening of the Vision Committee before committing capital funds.
